title: Which one fails?
examObjective: Defining, using, and reusing DataWeave modules, functions, and variables
basics: A recursive key rewrite has to be ready for every kind of value it might meet: Objects, Arrays and plain values. `mapObject` only accepts an Object, so calling it on an Array stops the script.
prompt: Each script upper-cases every key of the payload `{ "a": { "b": [ { "c": 1 } ] } }`. Three of them run. **One fails.** Which one?

options:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun up(v) = v mapObject ((x, k) -> { (upper(k)): if (x is Object or x is Array) up(x) else x })
---
up(payload)

%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun up(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((x, k) -> { (upper(k)): up(x) })
  case a is Array -> a map up($)
  else -> v
}
---
up(payload)

%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload mapObject ((x, k) -> { (upper(k)): x })

%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun up(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((x, k) -> { (upper(k)): up(x) })
  else -> v
}
---
up(payload)

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun up(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((x, k) -> { (upper(k)): up(x) })
  case a is Array -> a map up($)
  else -> v
}
---
up(payload)

explanation.approach: The failing version sends the Array under `b` back into itself, and the first thing it does is call `mapObject` on it. The versions that run either handle Arrays with `map`, stop at the Array, or never recurse at all. Two of those run but give the wrong answer, which is a different problem.
